claims.text: Partial routing gives a frontier lead model delegation guidance in its prompt, built from per-subtask quality and cost measured on past solo runs of both models; neither model is trained.
At delta=0.75, partial routing beats the lead alone on both benchmarks: on ViBench it scores higher at lower cost, and on Terminal-Bench it passes more tasks at similar cost.
Task-level routers, including a hindsight oracle, score lower than partial routing and cost more on ViBench.
Giving the lead only the profiled subtask plan, with no worker, cuts cost on both benchmarks and raises the Terminal-Bench pass rate.
Unguided delegation to a cheaper worker improves ViBench scores but does not improve the Terminal-Bench pass rate.
The judge's quality scores are stable across re-runs, varying far less than the gaps between the two models.
Raising delta shifts more work to the worker.
The authors hypothesize that the gain from workers comes from context management, since workers start with fresh contexts.
The gains carry over to a second model pair on Terminal-Bench, where partial routing passes more tasks than the lead alone at lower cost.
Profiling is cheap compared with training an orchestrator.

limits_authors.text: The main results use one model pair per benchmark, a small number of held-out tasks, and few runs.
It is untested whether the gains hold for model pairs with smaller capability or price gaps.
The method was tested only on coding and command-line workloads; transfer to other domains is untested.
Sensitivity to rho, tau and the number of profiling tasks was not studied.
The LLM annotator and judge were not validated against human labels.
The authors did not check whether the lead actually followed its assigned tiers.

likely_overclaims: The headline delta=0.75 is the best of three delta values, all evaluated on the held-out sets. No separate validation set was used, so the reported setting is effectively chosen on test data, even though the authors recommend sweeping delta on a validation set.
The Terminal-Bench gains rest on 23 tasks run twice each, so the difference over the lead alone amounts to only a few tasks, and no significance testing is reported.
Lower delta settings score below the lead alone on ViBench. This weakens the general framing that partial routing beats the lead.
The claim that the gains carry over beyond the main pairs is based on single runs. On the second ViBench pair, partial routing scored below the lead alone.
The large improvement on the profiling applications reflects leakage, because the judge saw their test results. The held-out margin over unguided delegation is much smaller.
The paper discloses that Replit, the source of the ViBench data, is a portfolio company of the authors' firm. This is a potential conflict of interest.
Calling the approach uniquely dynamic, informed and controllable rests on the authors' own comparison table, which uses their own taxonomy.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Partial routing. Offline, the lead and the worker each do the same tasks alone, and an LLM annotator then tags each step of their rollouts (gray) with a recurring subtask from a set \mathcal{S}; an LLM judge scores both models on each subtask, and \delta turns quality and cost saving into delegation tiers.
Figure 2: Cost and quality on the ten held-out ViBench applications, mean of three runs.
Figure 3: Cost and pass rate on the 23 held-out Terminal-Bench tasks, mean of two runs per task.

change_for_agents: Rather than routing a whole task to one model, profile your agent's logged traces into recurring subtasks with an LLM annotator and judge. Then put the resulting delegate/conditional/keep tiers in the lead's prompt and give it a subagent tool backed by a cheaper model. Even the subtask plan alone may cut cost, but expect longer wall-clock time when the lead delegates.

compact.claim: Guiding a frontier lead agent with per-subtask delegation tiers, profiled from past solo traces, beats the lead alone, task-level routing and unguided delegation in mean score, without training either model.
compact.method: An LLM annotator labels steps of solo lead and worker rollouts with recurring subtasks, and an LLM judge scores each model per subtask. Cost savings and quality risk are then compiled, using a parameter delta, into delegate/conditional/keep tiers placed in the lead's prompt alongside a delegation tool.

results.finding: At delta=0.75 on ViBench, the score rises from 70.2 to 78.5 at 19% lower cost; on Terminal-Bench the pass rate rises from 54% to 61% at similar cost.
On Terminal-Bench, partial routing passes 60.9% of tasks, against 54.3% for both the lead alone and unguided delegation.
On ViBench, partial routing scores 2.9 points above unguided delegation.
The subtask plan alone, without a worker, cuts the lead's cost by 39% on ViBench and 16% on Terminal-Bench.

compact.limits: Only one model pair per benchmark was fully evaluated, on ten held-out ViBench applications and 23 held-out Terminal-Bench tasks with few runs, and the LLM annotator and judge were never validated against human labels.
